purpose: Compare Autopilot research-selection policies under identical tools, evidence integration and call budgets, on synthetic scenarios with known ground truth.

policies.fixed-order: Rank first if incomplete, then every open gap in artist rank order (local, comparison, trends).
policies.random: Every open gap in a seeded random order; seeds 1, 2 and 3; results averaged.
policies.value-v1: Autopilot 1.0: single-gap materiality, justification and fallback tiers.
policies.value: Autopilot 2.0: joint materiality across gaps, budget-aware reachability, learned answer rates and batching cost.

developmentSeeds.use: Used while building and debugging the policy.

heldOutSeeds.use: Evaluated once after the policy was frozen. Not used for tuning.

closeCallFamily.reason: A 30-scenario development sample showed only 2 scenarios with jointly-material evidence; most decisions there are settled by ranking alone, so policies could not differ. This family is added before any held-out run.
closeCallFamily.definition: Scenarios from the same generator, kept only if at the start at least one open, answerable gap could change the bill alone or jointly within 4 calls (the jointMateriality test). The filter uses the starting state only, never ground truth.

generator: scripts/evaluate-research-policy.mjs#scenario: 5–8 candidates, 2–3 slots, shuffled full ranking, seeded fees and genres, 85% availability, 20% unquoted discoveries, 35% of evidence already known, 15% of scenarios start with an incomplete ranking. Ground truth per gap: local rows 55%; comparison 75%; trends rising 25%, cooling 25%, flat 10%, uninterpretable 40%; rank calls complete 85%.

metrics.agreement: Final recommended bill equals the bill chosen with every gap answered (full information).
metrics.regret: Full-information policy score of the full-information bill minus that of the chosen bill (0 when they agree; an infeasible choice scores 0).
metrics.interactionSubset: Scenarios where, at the start, at least one gap is decision-material only jointly with another gap.

fairness: All policies use the same research client, receipts, integration code, stop rules and phase budgets except where the protocol names a policy difference.
The value policies can spend one call on a location-free ranking cross-check; in synthetic scenarios this check cannot change the decision, so it is a pure cost to them.
Synthetic ground truth tests research selection only; it is not evidence about real Qloo responses or audiences.
